issues.description: extract_arch_from_url silently returns None and gets concatenated into a malformed URL
issues.detail: When the regex finds no arch, the function returns None and the f-string builds '.../latest/None/Packages/...', which propagates as a string and only surfaces as a downstream 404. Either raise on no-match or have the caller refuse to construct the URL. Don't swallow the failure into a synthesized path.

issues.description: nevra[0] indexes the first character of the filename, not the first letter of the package name
issues.detail: Koji's canonical path is /Packages/<first-letter-of-name>/<nevra>/. nevra here is the full filename like 'glibc-2.39-1.fc40.x86_64.rpm', so nevra[0].lower() works by accident today but breaks for names beginning with digits, punctuation, or any filename prefix. Parse the package name explicitly and derive the initial from it.

issues.description: Hardcoded arch list and koji base URL duplicate knowledge already present in the tool
issues.detail: The arches ['x86_64','aarch64','ppc64le','s390x'] and the kojipkgs base URL are baked into a helper with no module-level constant and no test. get_basearch is already imported; the supported arch set lives elsewhere. Lift these to a single named value so a future arch addition or path change is one edit, and add a test exercising the transform.

issues.description: Race condition with coreos-koji-tagger is documented in the commit message but undocumented and unmitigated in code
issues.detail: The synthesized URL is valid only after coreos-koji-tagger runs against the commit. That time-semantics invariant lives only in the PR description. Add a code comment naming the invariant, and at minimum log which URLs were synthesized so a failed Konflux build is debuggable without reading the commit history.

issues.description: Parse arch from the NEVRA suffix rather than regex-searching the entire URL
issues.detail: The NEVRA filename already ends in '.<arch>.rpm' — the authoritative source. Searching the whole URL with word boundaries admits ambiguity (a future mirror path containing 'x86_64' would shadow a noarch package) and may also drop noarch RPMs entirely. Split nevra on '.' and take the token before 'rpm'.

issues.description: Sloppy substring check for koji_url_base and redundant prioritization in query_packages_location
issues.detail: 'koji_url_base in url' will misclassify any future mirror whose hostname contains that string; use startswith or urlparse. Separately, the 'coreos-pool in url' prioritization in query_packages_location is now redundant since use_koji_url_only rewrites every URL — drop it or document why both layers exist.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this patch fixes a real DNF5 bug with a reasonable approach — synthesize the coreos-pool URL rather than trust upstream — but the execution has two clear defects that must block landing. extract_arch_from_url can return None and the caller concatenates it into a garbage URL, and nevra[0] takes the first character of the filename rather than the package name (works by accident today). Beyond that, the hardcoded arch list and koji base URL duplicate knowledge from elsewhere in the tool with no test, and the koji-tagger race condition is honestly disclosed in the commit message but neither documented in code nor mitigated by logging. Fail loudly on missing arch, parse the NEVRA properly, lift the constants, and add a test.
